Step-by-Step Audio Guided Tour: restaurant tour of Chart House, Boston, MA
Tour-Category: restaurant

Stop 1: Chart House

Coordinates: 42.3601, -71.0524

Orientation: You are about to embark on a walking journey through Chart House, Boston, MA. As you explore this single location, you will immerse yourself in the rich maritime history of Boston, intertwined with the innovative culinary creations of chefs honoring traditional seafood dishes with a modern twist. Chart House, an American seafood restaurant chain, traces its roots back to its inception in 1961 in Aspen, Colorado. From there, it blossomed into a national presence, with locations across Southern California, the East Coast, and Hawaii. Join us on this tour to uncover the fusion of heritage and creativity that defines Chart House. Your first stop is Chart House. This historic spot, housed in the Gardiner Building, stands as a testament to the rich maritime history of the area.

Chart House, an American seafood restaurant chain owned by Landry's, is one of 28 locations across the United States, including Boston, Massachusetts. The Boston location is particularly notable for its placement in the Gardiner Building, constructed around 1763. This building is steeped in history, having served as the counting house and maritime trading office for John Hancock, a prominent figure in American history. It was here that Hancock reportedly engaged in smuggling activities to avoid British taxes, a bold move that underscored the growing tension between the American colonies and the British Crown. On October 1, 1768, this very location witnessed a significant historical event when British warships anchored in Boston Harbor. The 14th and 29th Regiments of the British Army disembarked at Long Wharf, marching past. This act by British customs collectors, accusing Hancock of smuggling, led to riots and contributed to the eventual British military occupation of Boston.
